 Will There Be a ‘Nobody Wants This’ Season 4? What Netflix Has and Hasn’t Said
 Emma Loggins 
 Founder & Editor-in-Chief · October 22, 2026 · 2 min read 
 Follow 
 Table of Contents The Renewal Pattern Is Basically a Calendar 
 Season 3 Ending (Spoilers) 
 What a Fourth Season Would Actually Have to Do 
 Netflix has not renewed Nobody Wants This , and going by the streamer’s own record it has roughly two weeks to get around to it. All ten episodes of season 3 arrived on October 22. Finale spoilers are kept to the clearly marked section below.
 Nobody Wants This / Credits: Netflix 
 The Renewal Pattern Is Basically a Calendar
 Erin Foster’s show has been picked up twice, both times on almost the same clock. Season 1 premiered September 26, 2024, and Netflix ordered season 2 on October 10, fourteen days later. Season 2 premiered October 23, 2025, and the season 3 order came on November 4, twelve days after that.
 Run the same arithmetic against an October 22 premiere and a Nobody Wants This season 4 pickup should surface in the first week of November. That is a pattern rather than a promise. Netflix is entirely capable of sitting on a decision for months, or of walking away from a show people liked, and it has done both this year. But twice now the same two-week window has converted an October drop into a renewal, and a studio that repeats itself twice is usually measuring something.
 The other reason to expect movement quickly is that season 3 does not read like a series finale someone commissioned on purpose. It reads like a season written by people who assumed they would get another.
 Nobody Wants This / Credits: Netflix 
 Season 3 Ending (Spoilers)
 Spoiler warning: Everything from here down discusses how Nobody Wants This season 3 ends, including the finale. If you haven’t finished the season, stop here.
 What a Fourth Season Would Actually Have to Do
 Season 3 does the thing romantic comedies are structurally frightened of, which is let the couple arrive. Joanne and Noah end the season married, in an impromptu wedding on the beach in Malibu, with Sarah Silverman’s Rabbi Eden officiating. A Nobody Wants This season 4 therefore has to be about something other than whether these two can make the conversion work, and that is a much harder show to write.
 The material left on the table is the Sasha, Esther and Morgan triangle, which season 3 pointedly refuses to close, plus a family argument it walks away from mid-sentence. Timothy Simons, Jackie Tohn and Justine Lupe are the strongest case for a Nobody Wants This season 4 right now, and I say that as someone who has been sold on Kristen Bell and Adam Brody together since the pilot.
 There is also a handover question nobody brings up often enough. Foster and Craig DiGregorio ran season 1, then Jenni Konner and Bruce Eric Kaplan took the job for season 2, a change Variety reported alongside that first renewal. On a show that has already changed hands, renewed and the same show are two separate bets. FanBolt covered the season 3 trailer in September.
 If the clock holds, the Nobody Wants This season 4 order arrives in a Tuesday press release that almost nobody reads closely, and the interesting question stops being whether it happens and turns into who ends up running it.
